content.text: Everything the rule requires is present and at or above the preferred position.

input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: The indemnity package meets the preferred position in full. § 20.1 gives an unqualified Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims covering Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel; § 20.2 adds Vendor indemnities for breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. § 20.4 sets out standard procedure (prompt notice with material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense, control of defence, and settlement consent protections). Customer's reverse indemnity in § 20.3 stays narrow — limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with express carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or Vendor instructions. § 20.5 provides the usual infringement remedies (procure, modify/replace, or terminate and refund) as an addition to, not a substitute for, the defence obligation, and bars termination of unaffected Services. Indemnification obligations are also carved out of the liability cap as "Excluded Claims" under § 21.3, so the Vendor IP indemnity is not squeezed by the general cap and no 3× super-cap fallback is needed. Nothing here is one-sided against us; no redline required.
